messages:
Maya: Quick sync — we need a compact competitive narrative for next week's webinar and the field playbook. Focus: how Redwood compares to cloud AI endpoints, LLM APIs, and infra vendors. Can we sketch a short 3-point lead message + 2 rebuttals for each competitor bucket?

Tom: 3-point lead idea: 1) Predictable latency under load (SLO-first) 2) Cost controls (batching, quantization, routing) 3) Unified experience across hosted/dedicated/private. Short and product-y. :white_check_mark:

Javier: For benchmarks, recommend an e2e customer scenario instead of synthetic numbers — e.g., multi-tenant SaaS app, 10k qps spikes, p50/p95/p99 latency and "cost per 1M tokens" before/after optimization. Example stat to call out: `p50=80ms p99=320ms` on dedicated with batching. Link to draft numbers: https://redwood.internal/bench/drafts (perm: marketing)

Priya: Love that. For field one-pager we should include quick rebuttals:
- "We already run on cloud provider endpoints" -> "Those endpoints are flexible but opaque on unit economics; Redwood gives explicit levers (batching, KV cache, routing) + SLA-backed Dedicated."
- "We'd rather self-host with infra vendor" -> "Infra vendors give control but not the serving optimizations or eval tooling; Redwood pairs runtime optimizations with rollout + quality monitoring."

Tom: Add a short script for SDRs: "If low latency and predictable cost matter for your feature, Redwood reduces tail latencies with continuous batching and routing policies. We can run a 2-week pilot on your workload." Keep it <2 sentences.

Maya: Can someone draft: 1) 2-slide benchmark narrative (customer scenario + numbers) 2) 1-page rebuttal cheat sheet 3) 30s webinar opening line. Deadline EOD Friday. Who can own each?

Javier: I'll take the 2-slide benchmark narrative. Will add a simple chart + 3 bullet callouts.

Priya: I'll own the 1-page rebuttal cheat sheet and field Q&A prompts.

Tom: I'll try the 30s webinar open + SDR script.

Kai Bot: Reminder: marketing-assets channel requires drafts uploaded before 10:00 PDT on Monday for compliance review. :robot_face:

Maya: Perfect — drop links here as you have them. Also add one line for "most common objection" at the top of the cheat sheet (helps SDRs).

Tom: Quick copy for 30s open: "Customers choose Redwood when predictable application-level SLAs and cost efficiency matter — we give engineering teams the knobs to tune latency vs cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments." Thoughts?

Priya: Nice. Tweak: replace "knobs" with "controls" for sales tone.

Maya: Agreed. Last ask — can we surface one defensive stat vs cloud endpoints: e.g., percent of incidents caused by noisy neighbors or sudden quota throttles. Javier, can you see if metrics team has a number?

Javier: On it. If they don't have a clean metric, I'll use customer pilot anecdotes and label them as such.

Maya: Thanks all. We'll iterate here — pull in design once drafts are up. :rocket:
